item.title: Sokoto approves ₦6.12bn for nine UBEC model schools
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sokoto State Government has approved ₦6.12 billion for the construction of nine Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) prototype schools across the state’s three senatorial districts. The government also approved additional funds for the rehabilitation and construction of mosques and the development of Islamic educational institutions across the state. The approvals were among the major decisions reached at Wednesday’s State Executive Council meeting, presided over by Governor Ahmed Aliyu at the Government House, Sokoto. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Bashir Achida, said the nine UBEC prototype schools would be distributed equally among the three senatorial districts, with three schools allocated to each district. He said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to quality basic education, improving the learning environment and providing modern facilities for pupils, particularly in communities requiring better school infrastructure. Achida said the investment was in line with Governor Aliyu’s commitment to transforming the education sector under his administration’s Nine-Point SMART Agenda. On religious infrastructure, the council approved ₦221,548,705.25 for the rehabilitation of Achida Central Juma’at Mosque and ₦154,941,290 for the rehabilitation of Sabon Birni Central Juma’at Mosque. It also approved ₦98,242,007.50 for the construction of five daily prayer mosques in the Kwamberu area and ₦285,125,650.92 for the rehabilitation of Tureta Central Juma’at Mosque in Tureta Local Government Area. Similarly, ₦230,660,473.19 was approved for the rehabilitation of Kuppa Juma’at Mosque in the Gidan Sauro area. In the area of Islamic education, the council approved ₦166,982,489 for the construction of classrooms and sanitation facilities at Raddul Azzam Quranic School in Achida. Another ₦297,655,995.50 was approved for the construction of an Islamic school in Sabon Garin Tudun Wada area of Sokoto South Local Government Area. The commissioner further disclosed that ₦53,937,500 was approved for the provision of carpets at Gada Central Juma’at Mosque to improve facilities for congregational prayers. Achida said the approvals reflected the administration’s commitment to interventions in critical sectors, particularly basic education, religious development and community infrastructure. The projects, when completed, are expected to expand access to educational facilities, improve existing religious institutions and provide additional infrastructure for learning and worship across the state’s three senatorial districts. item.title: NASA Ames Stars of the Month: November 2026
item.description: The NASA Ames Science Directorate recognizes the outstanding contributions of (pictured left to right) Alyssa Villanueva, Steve Howell, and Samuel LeBlanc. Their commitment to the NASA mission represents the entrepreneurial spirit, technical expertise, and collaborative disposition needed to explore this world and beyond. Space Biosciences Star: Alyssa Villanueva Alyssa Villaneuva is an engineer at Blue Marble in the Space Biosciences Division on the LEIA (Lunar Explorer Instrument for space biology Applications) team. Alyssa is recognized for technical excellence, dedication and boundless support to the rest of the team. She goes above and beyond in contributing to LEIA every day and has been essential in all the test efforts, in particular with preparation and execution of engineering validation testing. Astrophysics Star: Steve Howell Steve Howell is recognized for his leadership of scientific teams for numerous international space missions. His pioneering work in astronomical instrumentation have significantly advanced both space- and ground-based telescope imaging. In kind, the Astronomical society has recently recognized Steve’s lifetime of major contributions to the field with the prestigious Catherine Wolfe Bruce Gold Medal from the Astronomical Society of the Pacific. Earth Science Star: Samuel LeBlanc Samuel LeBlanc is a research scientist for the Bay Area Environmental Research Institute in the Earth Science Division. Sam is recognized for exceptional technical leadership and innovative thinking in advancing Ames’ flight planning capabilities for NASA airborne science missions. Sam’s contributions have placed Ames at the forefront of airborne science flight planning within and outside the Agency, enabling successful and cost-effective missions that maximize scientific returns.

item.title: Edo pharmacists, consumer committee clash over drug inspections
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – The Edo State chapter of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has disagreed with the state Consumer Protection Committee (CPC) over the legality of the committee’s alleged entry into pharmaceutical premises to inspect and confiscate suspected expired, adulterated and counterfeit drugs. The pharmacists accused the committee of exceeding its statutory powers by conducting inspections, seizing pharmaceutical products and imposing fines on operators, insisting that the regulation of pharmacy practice is governed by federal laws. Addressing journalists in Benin City on Thursday on behalf of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN), an arm of the PSN, the state president, Pharm. Chris Oisakede, said pharmacists had established procedures for handling expired drugs in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Oisakede explained that expired medicines were not supposed to be discarded indiscriminately because of the dangers they posed to public health. “An expired drug is dangerous and poisonous, so they are usually gathered and handed over to NAFDAC, which has the protocols for destroying them,” he said. Flanked by other ACPN executives, Oisakede maintained that the CPC lacked the statutory authority to inspect, supervise or regulate pharmacy practice in the country. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Edo State CPC has no jurisdiction or authority, whether directly or indirectly, to enter, inspect, supervise or regulate the practice of pharmacy in Nigeria in any manner whatsoever. “Pharmacy practice in Nigeria, in all its aspects and ramifications, is governed by applicable federal legislation,” he said. He described community pharmacies as important healthcare facilities, noting that pharmacists counsel patients, promote the rational use of medicines, support treatment adherence, identify medicine-related problems and provide medicine safety information. The PSN consequently called on the committee to stop what it described as unauthorised pharmaceutical inspections, raids, harassment, seizures and sealing of premises, as well as the imposition of penalties where it could not establish clear statutory authority. However, reacting to the allegations, the CPC chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu, defended the committee’s enforcement activities, citing Section 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act as the legal basis for its operations. Iyamu said the provision empowered him to enter premises where there were reasonable grounds to suspect violations of the law, inspect products and examine their packaging, as well as take samples for examination. He added that the law also authorised the seizure of counterfeit, adulterated, banned or fake drugs, confiscation of unwholesome processed food products and sealing of premises connected with suspected offences. item.title: Children of Blood and Bone Trailer Features a First Listen to Tems’ “African Love Song” | Watch
item.description: Damson Idris stars as Prince Inan in the official trailer for Paramount Pictures’ Children of Blood and Bone. A fantasy world rooted in African mythology, a star-studded cast and Lagos as one of its filming locations: Children of Blood and Bone is bringing a major African story to the big screen. Paramount Pictures has unveiled a new trailer for the film adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi ’s bestselling fantasy novel, giving us a glimpse of Thuso Mbedu , Tosin Cole , Amandla Stenberg and Damson Idris in the fantasy adventure. Directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood , who co-wrote the screenplay alongside Adeyemi, the film brings the fantastical kingdom of Orïsha to life. The story centres on Zélie Adebola, a young divîner who sets out on a high-stakes quest to restore magic to her oppressed people. Alongside her brother Tzain, Zélie forms an unlikely alliance with Princess Amari and Prince Inan, the daughter and son of the ruthless King Saran, as they fight back against his tyrannical rule. item.title: Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)
item.description: null On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter , the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy , the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe. The new data release, designated DR1-Foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023 . The core of the Messier 81 galaxy group as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) "These are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," ESA's Director of Science, Carole Mundell said in a statement . "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration." What's in the Euclid release The ESA put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the Dark Universe Detective and contained in DR1-Foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars , regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes . "This is a change in scale from Euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," ESA's Euclid project scientist Valeria Pettorino said. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. This unlocks groundbreaking science." NGC 1291, a striking ring galaxy lying around 33 million light-years away from us, as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) Euclid can see such a vast number of cosmic objects thanks to the fact that its space-based position helps it avoid interference caused by Earth's atmosphere. This includes clusters of galaxies and even larger superclusters. The study of these objects, some of the largest structures in the cosmos, can reveal how matter came together across the larger network of gas, dust and dark matter called the cosmic web. "Euclid doesn't just look far back in time — it does so across huge areas of sky," Euclid Consortium member Barbara Sartoris of J

item.title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
item.description: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that's due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane. Read full article Comments

item.title: Pakistani astronaut set to become 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station this month
item.description: null An astronaut from Pakistan is set to launch on China's Shenzhou 24 mission in the coming weeks and become the first-ever international visitor to the Tiangong space station. A pair of astronaut candidates from Pakistan have been training at the Astronaut Centre of China in Beijing, following an agreement reached between China and Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 and a subsequent selection process. China's human spaceflight agency confirmed in a Nov. 7 press statement that the upcoming Shenzhou 24 mission will carry one of the astronauts. The agency also released a mission patch . "China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Nov. 9. "Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China's spaceships will mark the first-ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program." It is not yet known which of the two candidates will fly on Shenzhou 24. They were named in Pakistani press reports as Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, both pilots from the country's military forces. The pair were chosen from a wider pool of around 20 finalists. The chosen candidate will fly as a payload specialist on Shenzhou 24 along with two Chinese colleagues, while the other will be on standby as a backup. While the Chinese astronauts will be starting a six-month-long stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will spend roughly a week in orbit aboard Tiangong during a standard crew rotation period. He will then return to Earth aboard the departing Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with two Chinese astronauts who will have completed a six-month-long stay in orbit. The arrangement means changes to China's usual "three in, three out" Tiangong crew rotations. One of the three Shenzhou 23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong on May 24, will stay aboard and complete China's first-ever year-long stay in orbit, while the Pakistani astronaut will take their seat aboard Shenzhou 23 to return home. During his stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will be responsible for four research payloads selected from more than 300 proposals, according to Pakistan's space agency, SUPARCO. China has not announced a timeline for the launch of the Shenzhou 24 mission, but it is expected to lift off before the end of November. The Shenzhou 23 astronauts currently aboard Tiangong are closing in on 180 days in orbit, nearing an end to their six months in space. Shenzhou 24 will launch from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in the Gobi Desert on a Long March 2F rocket. The identities of the crew for China's human spaceflight missions are typically closely guarded, and will only be revealed in a press conference a day ahead of launch. Shenzhou 24's Long March 2F rocket will be rolled out to the pad around a week ahead of launch. item.title: Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26 Israel Discount Bank said Wednesday that from Nov. 26 it will let eligible customers buy, hold and sell bitcoin and ether in the bank’s mobile app, a launch that would beat larger rival Bank Leumi if it stays on schedule. The Tel Aviv-listed lender described the service as a first for Israel’s banking system in a Nov. 11 statement. Customers will be able to trade the two assets alongside stocks and bonds, without opening an account at an outside exchange or managing a separate digital wallet. The offer is limited to private, not corporate, customers who are Israeli residents, 18 or older, and whose accounts are already set up for securities trading, subject to the bank’s terms. “For the first time in the banking system, Discount Bank will allow trading in digital currencies directly from the bank account in a simple and secure manner, without the need for complex dedicated digital wallets,” Avi Levi, CEO of Discount Group, said in the statement. “This is a first step toward establishing advanced technological infrastructure in the digital currency space and developing the bank’s capabilities in this area.” The rollout was led by Elad Fisher, head of the bank’s financial markets division. Coins will sit in bank-provided wallets built on infrastructure from Fireblocks. JUST IN: $150 billion Israel Discount Bank will become the 1st bank in Israel to let customers buy, hold and sell Bitcoin Adoption! pic.twitter.com/gwKBy17cSf — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 11, 2026 A 2% commission and a wallet that does not leave the bank The bank’s product page lists a 2% commission on purchases and sales in the app, not including any foreign-exchange conversion. Custody fees are waived for six months from the Nov. 26 launch and then run 0.25% a quarter. Trading is open Sunday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 11 p.m. Israel time, and only immediate orders are allowed. Customers can buy as little as 0.01 of a coin. Holdings appear in the securities portfolio at once, with cash settling the next business day in U.S. dollars; conversion into shekels happens only if the customer asks. The service is a closed system for now. Bitcoin and ether bought through Discount cannot be sent to an outside wallet, and coins held elsewhere cannot be transferred in. The bank said it may revisit transfers later. It also warns of unusual risk, high volatility and the possibility of a total loss, and says the coins are not legal tender and lack the same protections as securities. What Discount is selling, besides convenience, is tax treatment. Capital gains and losses on the coins can be offset automatically against the rest of the customer’s investment portfolio for tax withheld at source, the bank said, at a 25% rate on profits. Sale proceeds land directly in the customer’s bank account, without the source-of-funds questionnaires that have often accompanied money coming back from

item.title: Microsoft has an image problem with November's Windows security update
item.description: Printing with Windows has always been something of a choose-your-own-adventure, and November's security update has added another unwelcome plot twist: documents containing certain images might not print. The issue affects images rendered with a height or width of zero at the selected printing resolution. These might not be visible to users, but can form part of a document's watermarking or layout. After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too. Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected." According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016. Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected. Users need not have added these objects themselves. Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible. Printer problems aren't the only issue requiring attention. After installation of the November 2026 security update, Microsoft warned that "certain Windows activation and licensing operations performed using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) might fail." This one is a little more niche, but it could be a headache for affected administrators. It primarily affects organizations that use command-line tools or automated processes to manage Windows activation and licensing. "Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008 , Invalid parameter ( SWbemObjectEx ), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said. "The failure has been observed while executing the command ' slmgr.vbs /skms-domain ' and ' slmgr.vbs /ipk '." The notice (WI1549486) currently lists Windows 11 23H2, Windows 10 22H2 and 21H2, and Windows Server 2025, 2022, and 2019 as affected. The printing problem remains under investigation, but Microsoft says a fix for the activation issue is due in the coming days. Administrators needing an interim workaround must contact Microsoft Support for Business. ®

item.title: JPMorgan Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 36% and Holds $540 Million in Bitcoin ETFs
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine JPMorgan Lifts Its Strategy (MSTR) Stake 36% and Holds $540 Million in Bitcoin ETFs JPMorgan Chase raised its Strategy (MSTR) stake 36% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Thursday shows, lifting the position to 848,932 shares worth $131.3 million at Sept. 30, weeks before an MSCI index exit. That is up 224,545 shares from the 624,387 JPMorgan reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at $57.87 million. Part of the dollar jump is the stock. Strategy’s implied price on the two filings rose from $92.68 at June 30 to $154.67 at Sept. 30, so the disclosed stake more than doubled in value even though the share count rose 36%. The same filing shows a much larger bitcoin ETF line. JPMorgan held 11,408,930 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $539.98 million at Sept. 30, up 1,001,295 shares, or 9.6%, from 10,407,635 shares worth $355.73 million three months earlier. Rounded to the nearest million, that IBIT line is the $540 million bitcoin ETF stake. Smaller positions in other spot funds added a little more. The bank also held 155,785 shares of Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust worth $5.76 million and 66,264 shares of the Bitwise Bitcoin ETF worth $3.00 million, plus much smaller lines in Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund, Grayscale’s Bitcoin Trust and Invesco’s Galaxy Bitcoin ETF. Together, the spot bitcoin ETF shares came to about $549 million. Option positions are listed separately and are not part of that total. JPMorgan filed a holdings report that folds in positions across 17 other included managers, so the Strategy and IBIT lines can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed those holdings since Sept. 30. The table lists 35,990 entries valued at $1.84 trillion. Executive Director Michael T. Lees signed the report in New York on Nov. 12. Options sit beside the share totals, not inside the $540 million The $540 million figure is shares only. JPMorgan also reported IBIT call options covering 3,703,200 shares, valued at $175.27 million, and put options covering 2,915,000 shares, valued at $137.97 million. The Strategy options are larger still, relative to the common stock. The filing lists put options covering 1,148,500 Strategy shares, valued at $177.64 million, more than the $131.3 million stock line, and call options covering 349,500 shares, valued at $54.06 million. A 13F does not say whether those options are hedges, market-making inventory or client positions, and they should not be read as a single directional bet. Other bitcoin-linked equities showed up as well. JPMorgan held 1,581,814 shares of Coinbase (COIN) worth $300.58 million, up 13% from June, and 128,788 shares of Strive (ASST) worth $3.77 million, a 179% increase in the share count. Bank of New York Mellon, in a 13F filed Nov. 5, raised its own Strive stake 28% to 237,100 shares. The filing lands as Strategy slides and bitcoin stays under $72,000 The Sept. 30

item.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
item.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. item.title: Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million Gemini Space Station has sold its already shuttered U.K. and European operations to Singapore stablecoin payments firm KAST for less than $10 million, according to CoinDesk reporting , as the exchange prepares to report third-quarter results after Thursday’s close. Gemini declined to comment. A spokesperson for KAST would not discuss the transaction, but said the company is actively looking at acquisitions as its revenue and footprint grow. Neither firm has issued a public confirmation of a sale, and no regulator has announced a change-of-control approval. The disposal, if confirmed, would close a retreat Gemini laid out in February. On Feb. 4, the Nasdaq-listed company, known as Gemini (GEMI), approved a plan to exit and wind down its operations in the United Kingdom, the European Union and other European jurisdictions, and Australia, as part of a broader effort to cut expenses and support a path to profitability. It said it would keep operating in the United States and Singapore. The plan included a reduction in force of up to 200 employees in Europe, the United States and Singapore, or about 25% of Gemini’s global workforce as of that date. The company estimated about $11 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, mostly in cash, and said it expected the wind-down to be substantially completed in the first half of 2026. Reuters reported the job cuts the same day. Co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, who started Gemini in 2014 as a bitcoin exchange, told customers the firm would “double down on America” after foreign markets proved hard to win and stretched the company’s cost base. Gemini later told U.K., European Economic Area and Australian customers that their accounts would close on April 6, with withdrawals-only starting in early March. What would change hands in a sale is the leftover entities, staff and regulatory permissions from those already wound-down units, not Gemini’s core U.S. exchange. Buyers of shuttered crypto businesses often want the licenses more than the remaining operations. Any transfer of a licensed firm in the U.K. or the EU typically still requires a change-of-control review by local regulators before a new owner can run it. A payments firm with European ambitions KAST is a Singapore-based financial platform built on stablecoin rails. In March, it said it had raised $80 million in a Series A round co-led by QED Investors and Left Lane Capital. The company, founded in July 2024 by former Circle executive Raagulan Pathy, said it would use the capital for expansion, licensing and compliance. KAST provides dollar-denominated accounts, cross-border payments and cards that let consumers and businesses hold, move and spend stablecoins. item.title: From Talking Drums to Tourism Diplomacy: How Nigeria Captured Attention at WTM London 2026
item.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing. Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world. It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it. Day Two: Tourism, Tradition and Private Sector Connections The second day combined cultural discovery with industry engagement, featuring a traditional palm wine experience, networking and interactions between Nigerian tourism stakeholders and international visitors. An important part of Nigeria’s participation was the presence of the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA), one of the foremost voices of Nigeria’s organised travel trade. item.title: The replicants are running the city in thrilling final trailer for ‘Blade Runner 2099’ (video)
item.description: null One of the most anticipated fall TV series, " Blade Runner 2099 , " recently dropped its final neon-tinted trailer, and now we’ve finally got a handle on the plot dynamics of this dystopian thriller set in the cyberpunk world of Ridley Scott's original. Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens. "In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis. "To secure a stable future for her brother, she assumes one final identity and is forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who’s confronting the end of her life. The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn." This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight! "You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop. Will "Blade Runner 2099" usher in a new era for the sci-fi franchise? (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099 " sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Delivered by creator and showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls"), and executive produced by Silka Louisa and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" lands on Prime Video beginning Nov. 25, 2026 .

item.title: Pan-African Vibes, Epic Bar Battles, and More! Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 was an Unforgettable Experience
item.description: The 12th edition of Africa’s biggest cocktail celebration, Lagos Cocktail Week (LCW), brought its 2026 theme, “Africa Pours into Lagos,” to life in spectacular fashion, delivering an exciting fusion of Pan-African creativity, cross-border collaborations, spirited competitions, and immersive experiences that celebrated the continent’s vibrant and evolving cocktail culture. Held from October 16 to 23, 2026, the week-long festival took cocktail culture beyond borders, bringing together some of the most exciting talents and bar communities from Lagos, Accra, and Abidjan. At the heart of this year’s celebration was a powerful message: Africa’s cocktail industry thrives when creativity, culture, and expertise flow freely across borders. The celebrations took off on Sunday, October 18, as the Italian Trade Agency brought a touch of Italian sophistication to the festival with the Italian Cocktail Experience, an exclusive, invitation-only masterclass and Aperitivo Italiano held at Mr Panther, Victoria Island. The experience offered guests an opportunity to explore the artistry and traditions of Italian cocktail culture. Speaking at the event, Maurizio Ferri , Director of the Italian Trade Agency, highlighted the initiative’s goal of promoting Italian wines and spirits, featuring brands such as Campari, Aperol and Martini. The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa , founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences. The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive , the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture. One of the most exciting additions to this year’s festival was the debut of the Lagos Bar Show, a fresh take on the traditional bar hop that brought the spirit of Pan-African collaboration directly into some of Lagos’ most exciting bars. On Tuesday, October 20, Sora Lagos played host to the first guest shift, welcoming the team from Bissa, Abidjan, for an exciting collaboration featuring Dodo Plantain Infused Rum. The following evening, Wednesday, October 21, the spotlight shifted to Praia Lagos, where bartenders from Accra’s Front/Back and No. 19 Bar & Restaurant brought a taste of Ghana’s cocktail scene to Lagos, with Audry Cognac taking centre stage. The guest bartenders took over the bar, creating a selection of signature cocktails with Audry Cognac as their base. Front/Back’s bartenders served the Mantse and Ashanti, while the team from No. 19 Bar & Restaurant presented the Akwaaba, meaning “welcome,” and Nkabom, meaning “togetherness.” Praia Lagos’ bartenders also showcased their creativity with Audry Cognac, serving the Audry Passion Sour and

item.title: United Airlines wants you to check in, not your chatbot
item.description: United Airlines has become the latest company to slap restrictions on unauthorized third-party AI agents, warning that the bots could make unintended purchases, expose customer data, or bypass checks requiring human acknowledgment. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Amazon has also moved against unauthorized AI agents, blocking Meta's Muse (the "AI that gets it done," according to Meta's marketing) in September . The airline has yet to respond. ®

item.title: BNY Mellon Raises Its Strive (ASST) Stake 28% to $7 Million as Monday’s 13F Deadline Nears
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BNY Mellon Raises Its Strive (ASST) Stake 28% to $7 Million as Monday’s 13F Deadline Nears Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) raised its stake in Strive (ASST) by 28% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 5 shows, lifting the position to 237,100 shares worth $6.97 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 51,544 shares from the 185,556 BNY reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $2.02 million. Most of the dollar jump is the stock. ASST’s implied price on the two filings rose from $10.91 at June 30 to $29.41 at Sept. 30, so the disclosed stake more than tripled in value even though the share count rose 28%. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. BNY filed a combination report that folds in holdings across its group, so the Strive line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. The bank oversees $63.4 trillion in assets under custody and/or administration and $2.2 trillion in assets under management, both as of Sept. 30. The Strive position is still modest next to other bitcoin-linked lines on the same report. BNY held 1,056,230 shares of Strategy (MSTR) worth $161.7 million and 162,072 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $7.67 million, a stake that nearly doubled from 85,282 shares at June 30 and is now about the same size as the Strive line. Monday’s deadline still has a few large filers outstanding Institutional managers that exercise investment discretion over $100 million or more in 13F securities have 45 days after quarter-end to disclose those holdings. That window ran to Nov. 14, a Saturday, so the deadline is Monday, Nov. 16. JPMorgan Chase filed its third-quarter 13F on Thursday. Wells Fargo, Millennium Management and Schonfeld Strategic Advisors had not appeared on the SEC’s EDGAR system as of Thursday morning. Those remaining names are among the larger managers whose bitcoin ETF and treasury-stock lines, if they report any, are not yet on the public record. BNY was earlier than most. It filed on Nov. 5, more than a week before the deadline, which is why the Strive line is already public while a handful of large managers are still unaccounted for. Other banks already disclosed bitcoin ETF positions Barclays, in a 13F filed Nov. 6, reported 3,942,900 IBIT shares worth $186.7 million at Sept. 30, up 48% from 2,658,147 shares three months earlier. Citigroup, in a filing dated Nov. 4, reported 521,144 IBIT shares worth $24.7 million, up from 347,114 at June 30, and a new $118.9 million position in Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC), or 1,636,387 shares, that did not appear on its June 30 filing. Those lines carry the same caveat as BNY’s Strive stake: a 13F gathers client, managed and trading-book positions, not proof a bank put its own capital into bitcoin or into a bitcoin treasury stock. item.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
item.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. The Vespera 3 also has CovalENS, Vaonis’s mosaic imaging system, which captures adjacent sections of sky to produce a larger image. That’s helpful for obj

item.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
item.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

item.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
item.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. item.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
item.description: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

item.title: Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Rumble’s AI pivot takes over The bitcoin drawdown came in a quarter dominated by Quake AI, the cloud and AI infrastructure unit Rumble built around Northern Data, the German GPU operator it acquired in June. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Executives said on the call that about $39 million of that came from writing up the value of Northern Data’s assets in purchase accounting. “Quake AI is now the engine of our business,” CEO Chris Pavlovski said. “We have real assets running real AI workloads for real customers and generating real cash.” The video business itself grew more slowly. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. Cash has been falling as well. RUM Group ended September with $134.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $203.3 million at the end of June and $237.9 million at the end of 2025. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. item.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
item.description: Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

item.title: BlackRock’s IBIT Bleeds $2 Billion in Nine Straight Days of Outflows
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock’s IBIT Bleeds $2 Billion in Nine Straight Days of Outflows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost another $269.7 million on Wednesday, its ninth straight session of redemptions, as U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a fifth consecutive day of net outflows totaling $299.8 million. Across the nine sessions since Oct. 30, IBIT has shed about $2 billion. The fund, the largest of the U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, has seen money leave on every trading day so far in November. The broader group has fared only slightly better. The 11 funds have lost about $1.44 billion over the past five trading days and roughly $1.88 billion in November, with outflows on seven of the month’s eight sessions. The lone exception was Nov. 4, when $74.6 million came in, even as IBIT itself bled $201.2 million that day. IBIT accounts for about $1.77 billion of November’s outflows, or roughly 94% of the total. Wednesday’s selling was concentrated. Besides IBIT, Grayscale’s GBTC lost $39.1 million, while Morgan Stanley’s MSBT was the only fund to take in money, about $9 million. The rest of the funds reported no flows. IBIT streak still short of this year’s worst The current run is not a record. Both the group and IBIT went 13 straight trading days without an inflow from May 15 to June 3, the longest outflow streaks of 2026. IBIT followed that with an 11-session streak from June 17 to July 2. Still, the size of the recent withdrawals stands out. IBIT’s two largest daily outflows of the year both came this month: $405.3 million on Nov. 2 and $403 million on Nov. 6. The selling has also flipped the year. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs are now down about $1.42 billion in net flows for 2026, compared with roughly $25.2 billion of inflows at the same point last year. The Australian Financial Review noted Thursday that the selling has erased this year’s net inflows into the funds. IBIT is still positive for the year, with about $2.45 billion in net inflows in 2026 and roughly $64.5 billion since it launched in January 2024. That cushion has shrunk quickly. IBIT took in about $932 million in October, and November’s withdrawals have already erased that amount nearly twice over. The withdrawals come just days after BlackRock argued that security fears were driving bitcoin whales out of self-custody and into IBIT. Why bitcoin ETF investors are pulling back The outflows began before this week’s worst headlines but have picked up alongside them. A hotter-than-expected October inflation report on Tuesday lifted bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and Polymarket odds of a hike climbed to about 97%, Yahoo Finance reported . Higher rates make cash and bonds more attractive relative to assets like bitcoin. Tech stocks have added pressure. Nvidia shares fell roughly 9% after Wednesday’s close following reports that its board was preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, and Nasdaq 100 futures slid with them. item.title: Bitcoin Price Falls Below $72,000 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down and Strategy (MSTR) Slides
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls Below $72,000 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down and Strategy (MSTR) Slides Bitcoin price fell below $72,000 on Thursday morning, its lowest level since mid-August, after Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang had resigned and Strategy shares slid following MSCI’s confirmation of an index exit, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The selling started after Wednesday’s close. Bitcoin slipped from about $74,700 to near $73,400 by 6 p.m. ET, then drifted sideways overnight. A second leg lower began around 6 a.m., and the bitcoin price briefly dipped to about $72,200 shortly after 8 a.m. The decline accelerated later in the morning, and bitcoin traded as low as about $71,670 around 9:29 a.m. That move pushed the bitcoin price below the low near $72,700 it set after Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected inflation report . It now trades roughly $31,200 below where it stood one year ago. Nvidia CEO steps down, and the bitcoin price follows Nvidia (NVDA) said Thursday that Huang has resigned as president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately. The company named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first board chair. Kress will continue as chief financial officer while she serves in the interim role. The board is searching for a permanent successor and said it will consider internal and external candidates. Nvidia is still scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter results on Nov. 17. The resignation follows reports of extramarital relationships, including one that has raised national security concerns in Washington. Sen. Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, had told CNBC that Huang should step down, saying he was “so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail.” Nvidia shares fell about 13% at Thursday’s open. Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.4% and S&P 500 futures fell about 0.7%, while Dow futures were nearly flat. Intel, Marvell Technology and Micron were down between about 5% and 7.5%, and CoreWeave dropped about 16%, giving back most of Wednesday’s 24.7% surge. Data center firms IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific also traded lower. Bitcoin price has moved with tech for most of this month. It fell on Monday when an earlier Nvidia probe rattled markets, then lagged Wednesday’s rebound in chip stocks. Thursday’s slide wiped out that small gain and then some. Strategy slides after MSCI confirms index exit Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, fell about 7% at the open after MSCI confirmed it will remove the stock from its indexes. MSCI’s November review removed Strategy from the MSCI USA Index , a step that also takes it out of the MSCI World and ACWI indexes, effective at the Nov. 30 close. Japan’s Metaplanet is also slated for removal. Index funds will sell MSTR shares, not bitcoin, and nothing in the rules requires Strategy to sell its coins. item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
item.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationship with another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. A two-week downfall News of the scandal first broke barely a couple of weeks ago, on October 29, when claims surfaced that Huang had been the target of an espionage plot involving a Chinese businesswoman working for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed which was a customer of Nvidia. According to the New York Times , US intelligence had reason to believe the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to gather information about Nvidia and its operations for the Beijing government. Megaspeed also faces claims it was illicitly shipping Nvidia products to China, in violation of US export controls. Any relationship between Huang and a Chinese operative would be enormously concerning, as the US has been trying to keep advanced technology for AI out of the hands of the country, allegedly for security reasons, fearing it might be used for military purposes. For its part, Beijing rejects the spying allegations, saying they are part of a smear campaign against China. Shortly after Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating Huang, he sent an email to Nvidia staff apologizing and confessing to having an affair, though he did not explicitly name Alice Huang in his public apology. It seemed like the leather-jacketed leader might just hang on, since it was difficult to imagine anyone other than him leading the company after all this time. But Nvidia’s shares fell 4.3 percent on November 9 and a further 5.5 percent the following day, wiping around $430 billion off its market value, amid all the speculation. Then the claim emerged regarding a second affair, with an employee at Nvidia who reported to him, and many commentators took it as a sign the game was up. Huang resigned the same day the news broke. Indecision ahead Now

item.title: ‘To them, we’re just NPCs’: the artists and activists challenging Trump’s video game propaganda
item.description: Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. After an explosion of news coverage, Arcade caught the attention of the games industry. The Tetris Company warned on social media that it “took copyright infringement very seriously.” Days later, the game was removed from the White House site. However, aside from a March 2026 statement from the Pokémon Company condemning the White House for using its characters in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) propaganda, major video game companies have been relatively silent in the face of the administration’s widespread usage of their IP. item.title: Vast data dump from Euclid space telescope reveals stunning galaxies
item.description: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The European Space Agency has just released a vast batch of observations of the sky captured by the Euclid space telescope. Launched in 2023, the telescope is currently on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to build the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos ever created . The latest observations – catchily titled DR1-Foundation – cover an area of the sky as big as 9500 full moons. The collection includes 900 million galaxies. The mosaic of 740 images at the top of the article, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, covers 367 square degrees of the northern sky. At full resolution, this snapshot runs to 500 gigapixels. Advertisement The bright oval in the lower left portion of the patchwork image is the spiral galaxy Messier 81, which is some 12 million light years from Earth. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Messier 81 in greater detail, along with part of the M81 group of galaxies that also bears its name – an honour bestowed on it as the largest galaxy of the bunch. To the lower left is the smaller galaxy NGC 3077, and the patches of wispy blue cloud throughout the images are galactic cirrus, which are actually in the foreground and part of our own home galaxy. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO Here, Messier 81 is shown in even greater detail, in an image taken at the full resolution available to Euclid. The haze dominating the right side of the frame is the disc of Messier 81, inside which individual stars are visible. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO This hazy galaxy is NGC 1291, around 33 million light years away. The image was made from two taken by Euclid and then cropped. In the background, even more distant galaxies are visible – the furthest away of which show up in red. Stars are still actively forming within NGC 1291, and can be seen as small blue-hued dots. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies lying around 800 million light years away. The cluster is home to a diverse array of galaxies, including whirling spirals and fuzzy ellipticals. In the centre of the image is a strong gravitational lens, where the light travelling to us from a more distant galaxy has been warped by a massive object in the foreground.

item.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
item.description: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Here are some of the best places to watch the moon's shadow cross what was once the Roman Empire. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Baelo Claudia, Spain Baelo Claudia's Roman ruins overlook Bolonia beach and the Strait of Gibraltar. (Image credit: Andrea Pucci via Getty Images) Location: near Tarifa, Andalucía, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:44 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 31 seconds Historical cloud cover: 12% Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east Roman ruins, an Atlantic beach and the mountains of Africa could all share the frame with the eclipsed sun at Baelo Claudia. Founded in the second century B.C., this remarkably well-preserved Roman city near Bolonia beach includes a forum, basilica, theater, temples, baths and a decumanus maximus (east-west street), all set against forested hills and a vast coastal sand dune. For photographers, the possibilities are exceptional — columns and temples may provide an ancient foreground, while wider compositions could incorporate the beach and dunes. On particularly clear days, Morocco is visible across the Strait of Gibraltar — potentially putting Roman ruins, two continents and a total solar eclipse into one extraordinary scene. 2. Málaga Roman Theatre, Spain The Roman Theatre at the foot of the Málaga Alcazaba dates back to the 1st century BC. (Image credit: Manfred Gottschalk via Getty Images) Location: Málaga, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 1 minute, 57 seconds Historical cloud cover: 9% Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east Few eclipse locations can offer two civilizations in the same photograph. Málaga's Roman Theatre was built in the first century B.C., when the city was part of the Roman province of Hispania, and today sits directly beneath the Alcazaba, the imposing Muslim-era palace-fortress that dominates the hillside above. item.title: Quantum leap: IBM plans to scale beyond 1,000 qubits in 2027 with Nighthawk r3 processor
item.description: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction.
